review_reference: UNSIGNED: reviewed_by stays empty until the owner signs under 0125. Owner decision Q92 B (single sign-on goes to production with password-only staff sign-in, as staff sign in today; the Q88/Q90 site rules hold; patients on app. keep working; the website switch VITE_HID_SSO is a separate release). Port of hid-system#142 (Identity single sign-on, ADR-070, written on main as 0102) onto production as 0125. Production has 0001-0123 applied. 0124 is reserved for the organisation kinds migration (Q90), built on another branch: this branch's pending migration is 0125 only, and it must merge staging after 0124 lands before release (until then the release contract refuses the gap at 0124 by design). Files: 0125_sso_relying_party.sql f7061195d9f38c668ce220d580fee81561fffd766964cc30610bca470950097a and runtime-grants.sql c3fca95d8afa03a24b29994f939e2ffea93d8810f23de16f6311ab76ea461dc9.
evidence: Migration 0125_sso_relying_party.sql f7061195d9f38c668ce220d580fee81561fffd766964cc30610bca470950097a (hid-system#142's 0102, renumbered; production has 0001-0123) plus its runtime-grants.sql block (runtime-grants.sql c3fca95d8afa03a24b29994f939e2ffea93d8810f23de16f6311ab76ea461dc9). WHAT IT DOES: adds auth.session_single_sign_on (one row per sign-in family a product issued after single sign-on: client ehr/lab/pharmacy/migrate/outreach/web, the provider sid, the provider auth_time; never the ID token) with the guard auth.guard_session_single_sign_on_change() (SECURITY INVOKER, search_path auth, pg_temp, no PUBLIC execute; admits only the root session of a staff or patient sign-in of the same account whose kind is the client's; refuses UPDATE and DELETE), an index on provider_sid, and auth.sso_spent_tokens (purpose transaction or logout_token, sha256 digest, expiry; single use) with an index on expires_at. Grants hid_identity_runtime SELECT, INSERT on the first and SELECT, INSERT, DELETE on the second, in the migration (production releases never re-run runtime-grants.sql) and identically in runtime-grants.sql; no other runtime role gets anything (post-check). The SQL objects are 0102's; only the number, header, precondition (0001-0123 applied, not already applied) and the grants block are new. No existing row, function, policy or grant changes; it reads nothing 0124 adds. Nothing uses the tables until AUTH_SSO_ISSUER is set. BACKWARD COMPATIBLE: today's identity-api never reads the new tables. The new identity-api serves no single sign-on route while AUTH_SSO_ISSUER is unset; it still reads auth.session_single_sign_on in the patient recent-sign-in check wherever 0125 is applied (so a family issued while single sign-on was on still counts from the provider sign-in after a switch-off), and on a database without 0125 it sends today's statement (to_regclass probe). LOCKS: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.sessions and auth.accounts for the two foreign keys until commit; behind another lock the runner stops after its 5 s lock_timeout with nothing applied. PROVED 2026-11-17 on throwaway PostgreSQL 16 clusters with fictional data only, deleted afterwards: (1) services/ehr-api/scripts/test-staging-schema-upgrade.mjs with a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS migrator: baseline 0001-0123 with production's runtime-grants.sql and the runtime-roles suite, plan exactly [0125], dry run rolled back, applied, checksums of 0001-0123 preserved, 0 pending, and a role bootstrap with this runtime-grants.sql changes no runtime privilege (2634 privileges compared), clean install of 0001-0125, row-level security unchanged on 206 tables; (2) the full synthetic rehearsal (scripts/tuf-staging-migration-rehearsal.mjs) as an unprivileged user, passed, including the new runtime verifier services/identity-api/scripts/verify-sso-runtime.mjs as hid_identity_api_runtime (a patient hand-off on the patients' site, a staff hand-off on lab. refused by the product gate with NO_ACTIVE_FACILITY_MEMBERSHIP, the same account's account-only session on outreach. bound to the outreach product, back-channel logout by sid and its replay refused, the ended sign-in's refresh refused as a denied refresh with no reuse_detected event, product sign-out from a browser with no sign-in left and by the refresh cookie alone, the patient recent-sign-in check counting from the provider sign-in with AUTH_SSO_ISSUER unset, product sign-out); the rehearsal needs release/node_modules and infra/cloudflare/node_modules installed (in this worktree they link to the same lockfiles' installs); (3) all 96 database suites (17 in database/tests including the new sso-relying-party.integration.sql, 79 in test/database) pass on a fresh 0001-0125 database; without 0125 the runtime-grants.sql block refuses (the tables do not exist). identity-api: build, typecheck, lint and jest (111 suites, 2905 tests) pass. Release checks: scripts/verify-migration-ledger.mjs passes; npm --prefix release test passes 95 of 98, the other 3 refusing only the missing 0124 prefix (components config.migration.files: missing migration prefix), which clears when this branch merges staging after 0124 lands. Dependencies (identity-api): openid-client 6.8.8 and oauth4webapi 3.8.8 added and jose 6.2.7 -> 6.2.14, exactly as hid-system#142; all pure JavaScript, so no new native file in the image (security/production-runtime-assessment.json unaffected); npm audit --omit=dev finds 0 vulnerabilities; the full npm audit lists 42 development-only findings today, against 43 for the lockfile before this change (the advisory list changes over time, so the count is the day's). RELEASE ORDER: 0124 (organisation kinds, Q90) is built on another branch; this branch must merge staging after 0124 lands, and the release then applies 0124 and 0125 in that order (0125 reads nothing 0124 changes; both add a block to runtime-grants.sql, so its sha256 here will change on that merge and this declaration must be re-hashed then).
